title: Indian Airlines Cancel Saudi Flights Through October 17 as Riyadh Airport Closure Is Extended
excerpt: A fresh Saudi NOTAM keeps King Khalid International Airport shut until 2100 UTC on October 17. Air India (Riyadh, Dammam, Jeddah), IndiGo (plus Madinah) and Akasa Air have cancelled services, with full refunds on offer — the third extension since the Houthi strikes began.
body:
• Saudi Arabia has extended the closure of Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport until 2100 UTC on October 17 (2:30 am IST on October 18) through a fresh NOTAM.
  • Air India has cancelled all flights to and from Riyadh, Dammam and Jeddah until October 17; IndiGo has cancelled services to Riyadh, Jeddah, Dammam and Madinah; Akasa Air has suspended Riyadh and Jeddah flights until October 17.
  • Affected passengers can take a full refund to the original payment source or reschedule at no additional cost; those who booked through travel partners should contact them directly.
  • The extension follows a second consecutive day of Houthi attacks on the airport — one person was killed and 11 injured in Sunday's attack, after 13 people, including one Indian, were killed and 208 injured on Saturday.

India's airlines have pushed their Saudi Arabia cancellations out to October 17 after Riyadh extended the closure of its main airport, the latest escalation in a week of disruption that has stranded travellers across one of the busiest corridors for Indian workers and families. Saudi Arabia issued a fresh Notice to Airmen keeping King Khalid International Airport closed until 2100 hours UTC on October 17, following Houthi attacks on the airport for a second consecutive day.

What each airline has cancelled

Air India announced that all its flights to and from Riyadh, Dammam and Jeddah stand cancelled until October 17, 2026, saying it is "closely monitoring and assessing the developments in the region to resume safe operations" and offering affected guests a full refund on cancellation. IndiGo has cancelled flights to and from Riyadh, Jeddah, Dammam and Madinah until October 17, according to the Indian Embassy in Saudi Arabia, which has been amplifying the carriers' announcements. Akasa Air extended the suspension of all flights to and from Riyadh and Jeddah until October 17, citing "the escalating security situation in the Middle East and the associated risks to safe flight operations," with refunds credited to the original payment source within seven days or free rescheduling for affected passengers.

The disruption is wider than Indian carriers. Air France-KLM has extended its Riyadh suspension to the end of October, Delta has postponed its planned Atlanta–Riyadh launch until March 2027, Etihad has cancelled Abu Dhabi–Riyadh services and 10 flights to Dammam and Jeddah until October 19, Qatar Airways has suspended Riyadh and Dammam flights, and Malaysia Airlines has cancelled Jeddah and Madinah services until October 17.

What travellers should do now

If you hold a ticket to Riyadh, Dammam, Jeddah or Madinah on any Indian carrier through October 17, treat the flight as cancelled even if your booking still shows as confirmed, and choose between the full refund and a free date change — do not simply wait for the airport to reopen, because the closure has now been extended three times. Keep an eye on the Indian Embassy in Riyadh's updates and your airline's app for the post-October 17 position, which will depend on whether the NOTAM is extended again. Travellers with onward connections through Saudi airports should rebook around the kingdom entirely until services are formally restored.
